Order the fleas $x_1\le\cdots\le x_n$ and set $d_i=x_{i+1}-x_i$. Repeatedly jumping the leftmost over the rightmost evolves gaps by $T:(d_1,\dots,d_{n-1})\mapsto(d_2,\dots,d_{n-1},\lambda\sum d_i)$, with characteristic polynomial $p(r)=r^{n-1}-\lambda\frac{r^{n-1}-1}{r-1}$.

**$\lambda<\frac1{n-1}$:** If $p(r)=0$ and $|r|\ge1$, then $|r|^{n-1}\le\lambda\sum_{j=0}^{n-2}|r|^j\le\lambda(n-1)|r|^{n-2}$, giving $|r|\le\lambda(n-1)<1$, a contradiction. Hence all roots satisfy $|r|<1$, so the span $S_k$ decays geometrically. The total rightward drift is $\lambda\sum_k S_k<\infty$, leaving every flea bounded above; no sequence of moves can pass arbitrary $M$.

**$\lambda\ge\frac1{n-1}$:** Then $p$ has a dominant root $r\ge1$ with a positive eigenvector. As $T^{n-1}>0$, Perron–Frobenius yields $S_k\gtrsim cr^k$ (and for $r=1$, the left eigenvector $(1,2,\dots,n-1)$ gives $S_k\to c>0$ whenever not all fleas coincide). Each cycle shifts the minimum by $\lambda S_k$, so $\lambda\sum S_k=\infty$ pushes every flea past any $M$.

Thus the condition is exactly $\lambda\ge\frac1{n-1}$.
